lead: >-
  The route through Chile, Colombia and Uruguay brings together the desert landscapes of the Atacama, the green hills around Guatapé and the shores of the Río de la Plata. However, the existing itinerary spends different amounts of time in these three countries and does not include a dedicated wildlife safari in each of them. The main days devoted to island wildlife take place in the Galápagos, in Ecuador, which is also part of the wider journey.

## Where to See Wildlife on a Journey Through Chile, Colombia and Uruguay

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current [32-day itinerary through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes the selected countries of Chile, Colombia and Uruguay alongside Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. It should therefore be understood as **one continuous journey with different highlights**, rather than a specialist nature tour confined to three countries.

The sections differ both in their landscapes and in the amount of time spent exploring nature. [Chile](/chile/) features the capital and a journey to the Atacama Desert. [Colombia](/colombia/) adds a visit to El Peñón de Guatapé and a reservoir surrounded by green hills. [Uruguay](/uruguay/) appears as a day trip to Montevideo, reached by ferry from Buenos Aires.

| Country | Natural highlights |
|---|---|
| Chile | Desert and mountain landscapes around the Atacama |
| Colombia | The rock and reservoir at Guatapé |
| Uruguay | Views of the estuary and urban waterfront |

**A dedicated, mandatory day of rare-wildlife observation in a national park is not specified for any of these three sections.** The "Wildlife and Safaris" theme is supported by the wildlife-watching activities included elsewhere in the full itinerary, particularly in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. Desert and mountain scenery belongs to the separate "Nature" theme. The clearest example of the journey's nature-focused experiences is the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador. Understanding the distinction helps you choose the right trip.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Chile: The Atacama and a Change of Natural Environment

After sightseeing in Santiago, travelers fly to Calama and continue to San Pedro de Atacama. The itinerary allows time to acclimatize to the altitude before traveling onward to the Bolivian highlands. The scenery changes dramatically along this section: urban streets give way to desert plains and mountains.

For anyone interested in the natural world, the arid environment, colors and geological shapes of the landscape, and wide-open horizons are especially compelling. There is, however, a difference between what you may see along the road and what a dedicated excursion guarantees. **The itinerary does not confirm a flamingo-watching excursion to Chilean lagoons or a visit to a particular nature reserve.** The lagoons visited on subsequent days of the four-wheel-drive journey are in Bolivia. It would be incorrect to place them in the Chilean section.

An evening astronomy excursion in the Atacama is offered as an optional activity. Whether it goes ahead depends on conditions and arrangements. It provides an opportunity to enjoy the desert sky, but it is not a wildlife-watching activity.

The climate calls for careful packing: dry daytime conditions require water and sun protection, while evenings may call for warm clothing. At altitude, a measured pace, acclimatization and attention to your health matter. It is sensible to discuss concerns about altitude tolerance with a doctor in advance.

## Colombia: Guatapé's Water and Mountains, Then the Cities

The Colombian section includes a full sightseeing day visiting [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), the town of [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and viewpoints overlooking the local reservoirs. For landscape photography, the contrast of dark rock, hills and broad expanses of water is striking. The route then continues to Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá.

The reservoir excursion **is not described as a birdwatching tour**, a mammal-watching activity or a specialist outing with a naturalist. It offers attractive natural scenery, but the Guatapé area itself is the main destination of the day. To look specifically for Colombian birds or wildlife, check other current itineraries and their particular parks in the [catalog of wildlife-focused trips passing through Colombia](/interests/wildlife/tours/colombia/).

After Guatapé, the program turns to cities: Comuna 13 in Medellín, the historic center of Cartagena, museums and Monserrate in Bogotá, and a visit to Zipaquirá. Mountain views around a city should not be mistaken for a promised trek in a reserve. The urban days offer a break from longer nature excursions, but leave less time for wildlife observation.

## Uruguay: Natural Geography Seen from the Ferry

It is particularly easy to overestimate Uruguay's nature component simply because the country appears in the itinerary. In this program it is **a one-day trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo**: an early departure for the port, a ferry crossing, a city tour with an English-speaking guide, free time and a return by the same route.

During the crossing, travelers see the vast Río de la Plata estuary; in Montevideo they see the city's waterfront. However, nature reserves, wildlife-viewing farms, hikes through natural areas and separate marine excursions **are not included** that day. Uruguay appears on this thematic page because it is one of the principal countries in a large tour that includes nature experiences, not because a safari is necessarily arranged there.

If Uruguayan wildlife is the main goal, choose a route with different stops and time specifically allocated to nature. Adding such days to an already packed eight-country journey could affect flights and hotels in its other sections.

## Where Wildlife Watching Actually Takes Place on the Full Journey

The most important difference between the complete tour and the selected three-country combination becomes clear later, in [Ecuador](/ecuador/). The itinerary includes [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), its [highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) and a boat excursion following **one of two alternative routes**.

The first option combines [North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) with Bachas Beach. According to the itinerary, seabirds seen on North Seymour include blue-footed boobies and frigatebirds; the day also visits the beach and lagoon area. The second option combines [South Plaza Island](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) with Cape Carrión, with sea lions and coastal wildlife. The specific option is confirmed after booking: **the itinerary does not promise both alternatives on the same scheduled day**.

For this nature-focused section, it is worth packing binoculars for birdwatching, lightweight sun protection and clothing suitable for a boat trip. Wildlife moves freely, so neither particular bird behavior nor a specific number of sightings can be guaranteed. National park rules require visitors to keep their distance from wild animals, never feed them and stay on approved trails. Breaking these rules harms both the animals and visitors.

You can compare Ecuadorian nature trips in the [selection of wildlife tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). Another useful comparison is [Chile, Ecuador and Peru: Wildlife and Safaris](/multi-country/chile_ecuador_peru/interests/wildlife/), where the Galápagos Islands are actually among the three countries selected.

## Why Regional Geography Matters More Than the Filter Name

Different natural areas require different amounts of time and different forms of transport. The Atacama and Guatapé cannot be connected by a short daytime transfer: on this tour, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador lie between them. Uruguay is separate from both nature-focused areas and is visited earlier, on an excursion from Argentina. Trying to compress these stops into a standalone "Chile – Colombia – Uruguay" trip without redesigning the entire logistics would make little sense.

For wildlife observation, the decisive resource is **time spent at a particular location**. A city stop lasting a few hours and a full island excursion with a guide offer very different experiences. The time of day, approved park routes, sea conditions, boat availability and seasonal animal behavior also matter. We help match the wildlife experiences you want with the days actually confirmed in the itinerary and explore which additional visits may be possible if the program is adjusted.

Packing for the different climates means combining warm clothes for the high-altitude desert, sun protection for the islands, a waterproof layer for the boat and light clothing for warm Colombia. The value of a well-planned kit is convenience between flights and excursions; large suitcases and delicate equipment also require attention to each carrier's baggage rules.

## Entry Requirements, Conservation and Expenses

Russian citizens and travelers holding other passports should check entry rules separately for every country and transit point. There is no single permit covering all of South America on this itinerary. The Uruguay excursion also involves **entering from Argentina and returning to Argentina**, making repeat border crossings relevant.

Chile uses the Chilean peso, Colombia the Colombian peso and Uruguay the Uruguayan peso; Argentina and the other countries on the complete journey have their own payment arrangements. Neither the acceptance of a particular Russian or foreign bank card nor the availability of cash exchange can be guaranteed in advance. Keep funds in reserve for actual expenses and check your bank's restrictions.

The Galápagos have additional procedures: a Transit Control Card, biosecurity checks on baggage and a national park fee. Confirm the current fees and which charges are included in your trip price before departure. Insurance for a nature excursion should also cover the actual boat journeys and other planned activities; merely having a policy labeled "medical insurance" is not enough without checking its exclusions.

## Who This Selection Is For

This selection suits travelers who want to combine a desert, reservoirs, South American cities and striking geographical contrasts in one long journey. Choose it knowing that **most of the wildlife observation takes place outside the selected three countries**, above all in the Galápagos.

If wild birds and mammals are the primary goal, start with the [general Wildlife and Safaris section](/interests/wildlife/) and compare the time actually allocated to natural areas. For the Atacama, mountain scenery and reservoirs, explore the [nature selection for these three countries](/multi-country/chile_colombia_uruguay/interests/nature/). If you want to keep the geography but change the theme, see [all trips for this country combination](/multi-country/chile_colombia_uruguay/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Nature in Chile, Colombia and Uruguay

### Is a safari guaranteed in each of the three countries?

No. In the selected itinerary, Chile includes Santiago and the Atacama, Colombia includes Guatapé and its cities, and Uruguay includes a tour of Montevideo. A separate safari in each of the three countries is not specified.

### Which natural sites are included in Colombia?

The itinerary confirms a visit to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and the reservoir near [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). It does not promise sightings of particular animal species there.

### Can I see Galápagos birds on this tour?

Yes. The full [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes an island excursion in Ecuador. However, only one of two routes is confirmed: North Seymour and Bachas, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión.

### How close can visitors get to wildlife in the Galápagos?

National park rules require visitors to keep a safe distance and never touch or feed animals. The park authority recommends staying at least 2 meters away. Instructions from the accompanying guide and the rules for the particular trail must be followed.

### Why is Uruguay listed under "Wildlife and Safaris"?

Because Uruguay is a principal country in an eight-country itinerary that includes wildlife observation in other countries, particularly Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. The Uruguay excursion itself remains a city visit.

## Chile and Ecuador: One Route Through the Andes to the Galápagos

**In this selection, Chile and Ecuador are countries visited on one extended journey, not necessarily two consecutive stops.** For this combination, we offer a [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It starts in Brazil, passes through Argentina and Uruguay, then continues through Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador before finishing in Colombia.

Our selection currently includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This matters when choosing a trip: "Chile and Ecuador" means both countries appear on the itinerary, but **does not promise a tour limited exclusively to those two countries**.

The Chilean part of the confirmed tour includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a flight to Calama and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The journey then crosses the Bolivian highlands, including [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), and continues through Peru toward Lima. The Ecuadorian section begins in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), followed by the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) and [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/).

## What Connects These Countries, and How Much Time Is Needed?

Chile and Ecuador bring together two very different experiences: discovering the Atacama Desert and exploring nature on the equatorial islands. A large section of the Andes lies between them, so the first decision is whether you want **a multi-country overland journey** or **a two-country trip with flights between them**.

| Option | How it works |
|---|---|
| Via Bolivia and Peru | Mountain sections and several borders |
| Chile and Ecuador only | Flights and fewer countries |
| Including the Galápagos | An additional island segment |

The first option is confirmed in the current [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The second and third describe possible structures for an individual request; the catalog itself does not confirm a ready-made two-country departure with those exact parameters.

In the itinerary running from October 22 to November 22, 2026, the Chilean section falls in late October and early November, and the Ecuadorian section in mid-November. When designing another journey, we help coordinate the order of countries, flights and a sensible number of nights near key attractions. The less time available, the more useful it is to select one natural highlight in each country rather than attempt to replicate the entire eight-country route.

## Why Altitude Makes the Sequence Important

Traveling from Santiago to the Atacama changes the conditions even within Chile. [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) is a starting point for desert and high-altitude excursions; the confirmed itinerary then continues onto Bolivia's Altiplano. Overnight stays and travel at considerable elevations may require acclimatization even for physically fit travelers.

After Bolivia come Peru and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). In Ecuador, travelers arrive in Quito, roughly 2,850 meters above sea level. A subsequent flight to the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) takes the journey into coastal conditions. **An extended stay in the Andes and a trip to the ocean call for different equipment and different pacing.**

Anyone who has struggled with altitude or has a heart or lung condition should review the itinerary with a doctor before booking. Check insurance for high-altitude journeys and remote locations separately, including altitude exclusions and medical evacuation. An ordinary policy intended for city breaks may not cover every section of this tour.

## The Galápagos: Separate Logistics Within Ecuador

The [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) are an archipelago reached by domestic air service from mainland Ecuador. The confirmed tour includes [Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and a boat excursion following one of two alternatives: North Seymour and Bachas or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. **The program does not promise both alternatives together**; the specific choice is confirmed at booking.

Visiting the archipelago involves special procedures: a TCT Transit Control Card, biosecurity baggage screening and fees for entering protected areas. Galápagos National Park publishes these rules separately from Ecuador's general entry requirements. When comparing prices, find out precisely what is included in the tour package and which local charges apply. The original 32-day itinerary lists admission tickets included according to the program, but the treatment of particular island fees is best confirmed in the trip quotation.

Biosecurity is particularly important: products of plant or animal origin and certain objects and materials may be restricted. Prepare a separate packing list for the island segment and check domestic flight baggage allowances. Compliance with the rules begins at the departure airport on the mainland.

## Documents for the Entire Journey, Not Just Chile and Ecuador

**Holders of ordinary Russian international passports must check entry requirements for every country they actually visit.** As of October 16, 2026, Chile's consular service publishes temporary-stay rules and a separate nationality-based check for the need for a visa in advance. Ecuador publishes passport-validity requirements and a list of nationalities requiring visas. The outcome may be different for other nationalities, second passports or different purposes of travel.

The current [eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also requires checking Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. Transit airports and the number of permitted entries should be checked separately. For example, the itinerary involves leaving Argentina for Montevideo and returning to Buenos Aires. Even where a country allows a short visa-free visit, that does not replace the requirements of neighboring countries or the border officer's decision.

Before payment, check passport validity for every leg, proof of itinerary and accommodation, onward tickets, restrictions in transit countries, rules on carrying medication and requirements for minors. Ada Tours helps align your documents with the actual sequence of travel, but visas and permission to enter are granted by the relevant authorities.

## Currency, Payments and Luggage: Two Different Travel Environments

Chile uses the **Chilean peso (CLP)**, while Ecuador uses the **US dollar (USD)**. A route through Bolivia and Peru also calls for bolivianos and Peruvian soles for local expenses. The fact that a tour is priced in US dollars does not mean that everyday purchases use the same currency. Souvenirs, tips, extra lunches and small purchases may require local cash.

For payment cards, the issuing country, payment network, restrictions imposed by the individual bank and fees all matter. Russian-issued Visa and Mastercard cards should not be assumed to work outside Russia; other cards also need checking before departure. Plan for an accessible cash reserve and legal exchange options. Do not assume every city will accept dollars at a uniform rate.

The weather varies as well. The Atacama is dry, with potentially cold nights and intense sunshine at altitude. Quito can be cool because of its elevation, while the Galápagos calls for protection from the sun, wind and conditions at sea. Pack layers, sun protection, comfortable shoes, a light windproof jacket and a small daypack. Check fare conditions and baggage dimensions separately for every flight.

## What the Actual Tour Includes and How to Choose

The [32-day, eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) lists 4-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers, excursions and admission tickets according to the program. International flights, optional excursions and personal expenses are listed separately. The cost depends on the accommodation arrangement and the particular product's terms; the price details on the tour page take precedence over an averaged figure for a country combination.

If Chile and Ecuador themselves should provide the main highlights, first choose two priorities, such as the [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Then decide whether to travel via Bolivia and Peru, how much time to spend on the islands and what pace suits you. Other country combinations appear in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Chile and Ecuador

### Is there a ready-made tour covering only these two countries?

The currently confirmed itinerary combines eight countries. The catalog title indicates that both selected countries are included in that route. A two-country trip with a different duration can be discussed as a separate custom itinerary.

### Is a separate permit needed for the Galápagos?

Yes. Visiting the Galápagos involves additional island procedures: the TCT card, biosecurity screening and a protected-area visitor fee. These are checked in addition to Ecuador's ordinary entry requirements.

### Which should come first: the Atacama or the Galápagos?

In the existing 32-day itinerary, Chile comes first, followed by Bolivia and Peru, then Ecuador. For a custom two-country journey, the choice depends on flights, dates, the length of the island segment and tolerance of high altitude.

### Can the entire journey be paid for in US dollars?

The tour may be priced in dollars, but purchases in Chile frequently require pesos, and other currencies apply on intermediate sections. Check whether your particular payment card will work and how to obtain cash before departure.

### Is additional high-altitude insurance necessary?

The policy needs to match the actual route and activities. The elevation of Bolivia's Altiplano and parts of the Andes, as well as the islands' remoteness, makes it important to check policy limits, exclusions and medical evacuation coverage.

## Chile and Ecuador: Adventure Across Several Countries

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The central offering is currently a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Chile and Ecuador are both part of its principal route, but Bolivia and Peru lie between them. The journey begins in Brazil and Argentina, passes through Uruguay and ends in Colombia after the Ecuadorian section.

This distinction is essential when choosing a trip. The itinerary **does not travel directly from Chile to Ecuador**. Its "Adventure" experiences are spread across several countries. The most substantial off-road segment takes place in Bolivia; the activities in Chile and Ecuador are different in nature.

## Chile: From the Capital to the Arid Landscapes of the Atacama

After [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the itinerary includes a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This marks a shift from city sightseeing to high-altitude desert terrain. The town is used as a stop before entering Bolivia, allowing travelers to rest after the flight and prepare for the change in elevation.

An evening astronomy excursion in the Atacama is offered **separately**, so it cannot be assumed to be included with every booking. The Chilean section of this tour also does not specify a demanding multi-day trek or technical mountain ascent.

What follows, however, is a substantial overland adventure: 4x4 vehicles cross Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, the Salvador Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers and Uyuni. Parts of the route exceed 4,000 meters above sea level, and the itinerary specifically mentions the risk of altitude sickness. **This adventure segment belongs to Bolivia**, even though it begins after a stop in the Chilean Atacama.

## Ecuador: A High-Altitude Capital and an Island Experience

After traveling through Peru, the journey continues to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) and then the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Quito includes a city tour and a visit to the equator-line area. In the Galápagos, travelers land on Baltra Island, cross the Itabaca Channel and continue to Santa Cruz. The itinerary includes a visit to the island's highlands and a boat trip along one of the designated island routes.

The boat excursion offers two alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas Beach **or** South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The particular option is confirmed upon booking. The tour description does not promise that the group will visit both options in a single day.

The island segment offers valuable nature watching, shore landings and guided visits. **Scuba diving, demanding mountain hikes and multi-day kayaking must not be added to the list of included adventures** without separate confirmation. Other types of activities can be compared in the [adventure tour selection](/interests/adventure/).

## Altitude and Flights: The Main Preparation Challenges

The principal challenges of this journey are the sequence of climate zones, changes in altitude and the large number of transfers. Bolivia's high-altitude regions follow the Chilean Atacama, then come the cities of Peru. Quito also lies at considerable elevation, whereas the Galápagos is an island segment near the equator.

To understand the demands, divide the journey into three parts:

| Section | What affects the level of exertion |
|---|---|
| Chile | Flights and the Atacama's dry climate |
| Bolivia and Peru | Altitude, 4x4 trips and road transfers |
| Ecuador | Flights and marine excursions |

Allow time for sleep and acclimatization, and bring comfortable shoes, sun protection and clothing for changing temperatures. On the islands, follow protected-area rules and local guides' instructions. Anyone with medical limitations should assess the suitability of the high-altitude itinerary in advance.

## Who This Combination Suits

This route suits travelers eager to experience the contrast between the dry Atacama, the high Andes and equatorial islands, who are comfortable with frequent transfers and accept that some excursions are organized in groups. Its length allows for variety, but does not turn every day into an active sporting adventure.

If physical exertion is the priority, specify the activities you want before choosing the itinerary: trekking, mountaineering, kayaking, cycling or diving. Then check on which day, and under which conditions, each is actually available. This page presents [tours passing through Chile and Ecuador](/multi-country/chile_ecuador/) with an adventure theme; it does not promise every possible outdoor activity on request.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Adventure in Chile and Ecuador

### Can you travel directly from Chile to Ecuador?

In the existing 32-day itinerary, Bolivia and Peru lie between them. A direct connection would require a different program and a separate calculation of flights.

### Where is the most demanding section?

The four-wheel-drive journey through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons includes sections above 4,000 meters. It is particularly important here to assess your ability to cope with altitude and long vehicle journeys in advance.

### Are diving and trekking included in the Galápagos?

The confirmed program includes island and boat excursions. Scuba diving and demanding sports trekking are not listed as included services.

### When is the island route decided?

The Galápagos boat excursion offers two alternative itineraries. The specific island route is confirmed after booking; both cannot be promised together.

## The Culture of Chile and Ecuador on One Journey

This selection currently includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Chile and Ecuador are two required countries on this longer route. Travelers pass through Bolivia and Peru between [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/).

The cultural itinerary is therefore a sequence of different historic cities rather than a short trip to just two capitals. In Chile, the focus is on Santiago's urban history and public spaces. In Ecuador, it is on old Quito and attractions connected with the equator line. The richest archaeological experiences occur in the intervening Peruvian and Bolivian sections.

## Santiago: The Square, the Palace and the City Neighborhoods

Following arrival in the Chilean capital, the itinerary includes a group sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide. It covers the historic center, including the [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/) area and a view of the exterior architecture of [La Moneda Palace](/chile/place/la-moneda-palace/), together with other city neighborhoods along the sightseeing route.

The point of this stop is to experience the administrative and historic center of modern Chile before the country gives way to desert landscapes. The next stage involves a flight to Calama and a journey toward [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), followed by the high-altitude landscapes of Bolivia.

A culture-related label on the wider tour does not mean that every museum in Santiago is included: the confirmed itinerary should be read in terms of the actual sightseeing day. Free time and optional visits should likewise be distinguished from the included excursion.

## Between the Capitals: The History of the Andes

The countries between Chile and Ecuador explain why a longer itinerary can be more rewarding than simply flying from Santiago to Quito. In Bolivia the journey includes [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), and in Peru it visits [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The route across the Andes brings together monuments from different historical periods and modern cities.

The confirmed program includes travel toward Lake Titicaca, visits to Inca heritage sites near Cusco, an excursion to Machu Picchu and then a flight from Lima to Quito. This provides time to explore archaeological attractions, but also involves significant travel and high-altitude sections. If you are interested only in Chile and Ecuador, much of the 32-day journey may be unnecessary.

## Quito: Historic Architecture and the Equator Line

The Ecuadorian section begins with an introduction to Quito. Sightseeing covers urban architecture and panoramic views as well as the equator-line area, including Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum. It combines the capital's architectural history with a geographical theme that is particularly interesting to discuss with a guide on site.

The journey then continues to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where attention turns to nature and marine excursions. If your focus is culture, expectations need to be set accordingly: the island segment **is not a continuation of a series of urban museums**. It offers a different experience and requires separate logistics.

If architecture, history and archaeology matter most, compare [cultural and historical trips in Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/) with [cultural and historical trips in Ecuador](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/) and then decide whether to include the other countries.

**The most striking contrast in this combination is between Chile's arid highlands and Ecuador's protected island ecosystems.** On the current itinerary, however, Bolivia and Peru lie between these two experiences. That determines the actual flights, duration and time travelers spend in each natural area.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The relevant itinerary is [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). ## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as a Stop on a High-Altitude Route

After Santiago, the group flies to [Calama](/chile/place/calama/) and transfers to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), an oasis town surrounded by desert. Altitude, humidity, temperatures and walking conditions change here, particularly compared with the city days spent in the earlier countries.

However, **the approved itinerary uses San Pedro primarily for acclimatization** before entering Bolivia's highlands. A nighttime astronomy excursion is offered separately. The town's presence on the route does not mean that trips to every geyser, Chilean salt flat or popular Atacama valley are automatically included.

A four-wheel-drive trip through Bolivia follows, with high-altitude lagoons, hot springs and the Uyuni Salt Flat. The principal natural sites on this section lie beyond the Chilean border. This distinction matters to travelers specifically looking to explore Chile's nature: a stop in San Pedro and several days of Atacama excursions are fundamentally different products.

If immersing yourself in desert landscapes is the main goal, look at [nature tours in Chile](/interests/nature/tours/chile/) and compare their included activities.

Later, the journey continues through Peru into Ecuador. Travelers first explore Quito before flying to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Arrival via Baltra leads to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), where the program includes island stops and an introduction to the archipelago's landscapes.

The following day offers **two alternative routes, only one of which is taken**. The first option includes North Seymour and Bachas Beach; the second includes South Plaza and Cape Carrión. For nature enthusiasts, this is an important difference: different islands and stretches of coast provide different wildlife-watching conditions. Landing restrictions, sea conditions and national park rules may influence the chosen excursion. Encounters with particular animals cannot be guaranteed.

Protected-area regulations apply throughout the Galápagos: visitors must keep their distance from animals, never feed them, remain on authorized trails and use approved tourist services. Following these rules protects the natural environment and reduces risks for visitors.

## Why Climate and Duration Call for Different Choices

The Atacama's dry air combines with strong sunshine and cool nights. In the Galápagos, sea breezes, boating conditions and sun exposure on the water matter more. Pack for two very different environments: a warm windproof layer and other layers for high elevations, and light clothing and sun protection for the islands.

An even more significant consideration is the long interval between Chile and Ecuador. Travelers cross Bolivia's high-altitude regions and then visit Peruvian cities and Machu Picchu. If you want a journey **limited to Chile and Ecuador**, removing the other countries would require completely different logistics, flights and timing. The existing 32-day tour cannot be treated as a 7–10-day itinerary whose intervening countries can simply be removed at will.

Pay particular attention to alternating elevations and physical demands. Travelers whose medical conditions might complicate a stay at high altitude should discuss that part of the route with a doctor. Galápagos boat excursions have different restrictions related to sea conditions and park regulations.
